Subaru Launches All-New E-Outback in the UK From £49,995, It's America's Trailseeker, Actually
9 photos
Photo: Subaru
It's also known as the Toyota bZ4X Touring or bZ Woodland if you don't want it as the Subaru Trailseeker or E-Outback - the Japanese love to confuse us when it comes to all-electric models.
Although usually both the Toyota and Subaru lineups are pretty easy to understand, somehow the series of battery-electric compact crossover SUVs offered by both Toyota and Subaru based on the e-TNGA platform ended up more confusing than explaining why we cook bacon and bake cookies or how long does someone have to be dead before ‘looting’ their remains becomes archaeology instead of grave robbing…
So, Toyota introduced their first all-electric model based on the co-developed e-TNGA platform as the bZ4X, while Subaru named it Solterra. Lexus also offers their premium version, dubbed RZ. Anyway, now in America this model is known simply as bZ, while in Europe it remains as the bZ4X.
Wait, wait, we’re not done – there are also two long-wheelbase models known as the bZ Woodland and Subaru Trailseeker in North America, but alternatively as the bZ4X Touring and Subaru E-Outback on the Old Continent. Confusing and unnecessary, right?
Anyway, now that you know about the E-Outback, the new model is coming to the United Kingdom with the “stylish practicality, safety and off-road capabilities of the Outback” nameplate but with zero emissions. It comes to the market in four guises: All-Wheel Drive (AWD), Field, Touring, and Touring +, with pricing starting from £49,995 OTR (that’s over $65k at the current exchange rate).
First customer deliveries are scheduled for early next year, and the Subaru E-Outback is produced at Subaru’s newly upgraded Gunma Yajima Plant in Japan, rocking Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive (S-AWD) and a 74.7 kWh Lithium-ion battery pack along with dual motors. The combined output is 280 kW/381 PS or 376 hp and 536 Nm or 395 lb-ft of torque, with the model sprinting to 62 mph in 4.5 seconds and reaching a top speed of 111 mph or 179 kph.
The entry-level AWD model has a WLTP range of up to 325 miles or 523 km while the other versions have a WLTP rating of up to 300 miles (483 km) and the Subaru E-Outback also comes with a dual-function X-MODE system, 210mm (8.26 inches) of ground clearance, and a luggage capacity of 633 liters (22.35 cubic feet), expandable through the 60:40 split bench to 1,230 liters – or 43.43 cu. ft.
The capability specifications in the UK also include a braked towing capacity of up to 1,500 kg (3,307 pounds), and inside customers will find both wireless Apple CarPlay and wired Android Auto, two wireless phone chargers, USB-C ports front and rear, a 220-volt AC power outlet in the trunk, as well as standard dual-zone climate control and a Harman Kardon sound system on the Field, Touring, and Touring + models.
